topStories.headline: Grand Lake Kitchen Settles Into Noe Valley, Winning Over the Neighborhood
topStories.dek: The East Bay comfort-food favorite has firmly planted its flag in the former Mr. Digby's space on Church Street.
topStories.body:
Grand Lake Kitchen, the beloved Oakland all-day café and bistro from owners May Seto Wasem and Dave Wasem, has become one of Noe Valley's most talked-about new arrivals since its soft opening in March 2026. The restaurant — the couple's third location and their first in San Francisco — took over the refurbished space at 1199 Church Street that formerly housed Mr. Digby's Bar and Restaurant, and before that, Noe's Cantina.

The Mission Local, which revisited the restaurant in August, described the space as bustling and high-spirited, with hanging plants, copper lamps, and an inviting atmosphere that felt like a party from the moment guests arrived. The Noe Valley location features a spacious dining room, full bar, two outdoor patios, and a private dining room.

The Wasems — who are no strangers to SF, as May spent years in Noe Valley post-college — said the neighborhood's strong residential demand base and foot traffic on 24th Street made the bet on San Francisco pencil out. The restaurant began operating seven days a week in April, with menu highlights including caviar pie, a reuben, chilaquiles verdes, pastrami benedict, steak frites, and eggplant parmesan.

The opening is part of a broader uptick in commercial activity on 24th Street and in Noe Valley more broadly, as outside operators increasingly choose the neighborhood over suburban East Bay expansion routes. Community observers note that the Noe Valley Town Square has quietly become a civic anchor that helps make those bets viable.

topStories.headline: Castro Theatre Keeps Its Summer Calendar Full After Landmark Reopening
topStories.dek: Six months after its $41 million renovation debut, the historic Castro Theatre is operating at full speed with a packed lineup through fall.
topStories.body:
The Castro Theatre, which reopened in February 2026 following a $41 million renovation and restoration by Another Planet Entertainment (APE), has continued to draw audiences through summer with a diverse mix of live music, comedy, and film. This week, the venue hosts Imperial Teen for a sold-out two-night run on Saturday and Sunday, August 22–23, before transitioning into an end-of-August concert on Friday, August 28.

The 1922 Spanish Baroque Revival building had been dark since February 2024 while APE undertook extensive upgrades, including restored ceiling artwork, a reinstalled chandelier, improved accessibility, expanded restrooms, and a new motorized seating system that allows the auditorium to shift between film screenings and concert configurations.

APE, which also operates the Bill Graham Civic Auditorium and Berkeley's Greek Theatre, has programmed the venue with a wide range of acts since its reopening debut with a Sam Smith residency. The Frameline LGBTQ+ Film Festival also returned to the Castro in 2026, fulfilling the organization's hopes to reclaim its longtime home.

Neighborhood business owners have credited the reopening with helping revive foot traffic in the Castro. Looking ahead, country artist Orville Peck is scheduled for a Saturday, September 12 show, and the venue has dates booked into November 2026.
topStories.sourceName: Local News Matters / Bay City News

topStories.headline: Bank Robbery at Diamond Heights Branch of Bank of America; Investigation Under Way
topStories.dek: A person robbed the Bank of America in Diamond Heights on August 10 and fled with cash; the SFPD Bank Robbery Unit is investigating.
topStories.body:
A robbery occurred on Monday, August 10, at approximately 2:30 p.m. at the Bank of America branch in Diamond Heights. According to the Glen Park Association, which reported the incident, one person robbed the branch and left with an undisclosed amount of money. No injuries were reported.

The San Francisco Police Department responded to the scene. According to the Glen Park Association's report, the SFPD has a good description of the suspect. The case was subsequently transferred to the SFPD Bank Robbery Unit for further investigation.

Residents in the Diamond Heights and Glen Park areas are encouraged to remain vigilant and report any suspicious activity. Anyone with information related to this incident is asked to contact the SFPD Tip Line at 1-415-575-4444, or to text a tip to TIP411 with the keyword SFPD.

Free with suggested donation of $10–$20; proceeds support community beneficiaries.

moreNews.headline: Castro Merchants Track New Business Wave as Neighborhood Rebounds
moreNews.body: A February 2026 report from the Bay Area Reporter documented a wave of new businesses opening in the Castro alongside the historic Castro Theatre's reopening. New entrants included Gada, a Tunisian-American sandwich shop offering raclette cheese sandwiches on mlewi flatbread, and plans by LGBTQ proprietor Jacob Paronyan to open American bistro Parasol at Flore in the former Cafe Flore space at 2298 Market Street. Castro Merchants Association president Nate Bourg said the neighborhood is beginning to feel the pre-pandemic buzz again, and the theatre's projected 200,000-plus annual visitors are expected to benefit surrounding restaurants and retail.

moreNews.headline: BART Schedule Changes May Affect Glen Park Commuters
moreNews.body: BART updated its service schedule on August 10, 2026, implementing longer trains and operational efficiencies aimed at reducing delays and crowding system-wide. Riders using the Glen Park BART station, one stop south of 24th Street Mission, should check sfmta.com and bart.gov for the latest service information. Separately, changes to the 35 and 36 bus lines serving Glen Park and Diamond Heights have been in effect since June, with updated stop details posted by the SFMTA.

moreNews.headline: Castro Night Market Closes Out 2026 Season with September 18 Finale
moreNews.body: The Castro Night Market, which launched its second season in March 2026, will hold its final installment of the year on Friday, September 18, from 5 to 10 p.m. on 18th Street between Hartford and Collingwood. The monthly market, presented by CG Events, the Castro Merchants Association, and the Civic Joy Fund, has featured local food vendors, makers, drag performances, and live entertainment each third Friday from March through September. The August 21 edition — happening tonight — honors local community leaders who have shaped the neighborhood.

moreNews.headline: Noe Valley Real Estate Continues Record Pace Into Summer 2026
moreNews.body: A May 2026 SF Standard feature reported that Noe Valley has solidified its position as one of San Francisco's most expensive residential markets, with starter homes frequently listing around $3 million. Analysts and community observers attribute the neighborhood's resilience to decades of resident and merchant investment in family-friendly amenities, public spaces like the Town Square, and a safe, village-like environment. The trend is now drawing commercial operators — including Grand Lake Kitchen — who are choosing Noe Valley over lower-cost suburban expansion alternatives.
